_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4464 — the two driver-reliability guards the four out-of-jest `*-pipe.harness.ts` files now share (`helpers/pipe-harness-guards.ts`). Subject is the HELPER because that is where the guards live after the consolidation: a mutant anchored in one harness could only speak for that harness, whereas one anchored here speaks for all four at once (integration-test-revert-verify §A117 — the mutant travels with the guard to its new carrier). The WIRING half — that each harness actually goes through the helper — is a separate subject and lives in pipe-harness-guards-4464.wiring.spec.json. ⛤ Unlike the four sibling `*.pipe.spec.json` files this one is CI-gated: its axes are plain fs/argv logic, so they run in `test-coverage-cli` even though the harnesses they protect cannot (the CLI jest job does not build `dist`). Expectation written BEFORE the run. Both defects were OBSERVED on the real tree first: `touch packages/cli/src/index.ts` + `--no-build` measured the pre-touch bundle in silence before the fix and refuses with `dist older than src … predates …` after it.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/tests/integration/helpers/pipe-harness-guards.ts

M1_staleness_refusal_dropped._note: Keeps the staleness COMPUTATION and drops only the refusal — the shape `--no-build` had before #4464, where the sole check was `fs.existsSync(DIST)`. G1 reddens because `prepareBundle` then returns the stale bundle instead of throwing. G2 stays GREEN (a bundle newer than its inputs was always allowed through, so a guard that never refuses cannot be told from a correct one there) and G2b stays GREEN (the missing-bundle refusal is a separate throw, which is what says the staleness check did not simply subsume it). That pair is the control: without it, one red axis could not distinguish `--no-build` being broken outright from the staleness half being gone.

M2_cleanup_out_of_finally._note: Exactly the pre-#4464 shape: cleanup as the last statement of the happy path rather than a `finally`, so a throwing axis leaks its temp tree under os.tmpdir() (LOW from the #4462 review). Type-preserving — the function still returns `Promise<T>` — because a mutant that failed to compile would print `Tests: 0` and read as `the axis does not differentiate` instead of as a lost guard (integration-test-revert-verify §A36/§A97). G3 reddens on its `existsSync === false` half; its `rejects.toThrow` half stays satisfied, which is what says the mutant removed the CLEANUP rather than the error propagation.

M3_symlinked_inputs_invisible._note: Classifies each entry by its `Dirent` kind instead of by a following `statSync` — the obvious shape, and the one this module shipped with in its first round. A Dirent for a symlink answers false to BOTH isDirectory and isFile (measured), so the whole symlinked subtree is skipped and the staleness check hands back `null` however old the bundle is. Only G8 reddens: G9 and G10 stay GREEN because a dirent-kind walk also skips a dangling symlink and a loop symlink — which is exactly why those two axes cannot stand in for this one, and why the guard needed three axes rather than one.

M4_stat_race_unguarded._note: Follows symlinks but drops the guard around the follow. A dangling symlink then throws ENOENT out of the walk, past `distStalenessReason` and `prepareBundle`, and `prepareBundleOrExit` rethrows anything that is not a PipeHarnessBundleError — so the harness dies with a raw stack trace instead of its `❌ BUILD — …` line. The same guard covers the TOCTOU case a dangling link stands in for deterministically: a file listed by readdirSync and removed before its statSync by a concurrent build under `dist/`. ⛤ G10 reddens TOO, and that was NOT the prediction — it was written from the mutant's theme (`ENOENT`) rather than from which axes actually execute after it (integration-test-revert-verify §A44). Measured cause: inside a symlink loop it is `statSync` that raises ELOOP first, at the same depth `readdirSync` would, so this one guard absorbs BOTH the unresolvable entry and the loop. `expect` was widened only after reading why, not to make the run pass. G8 stays GREEN — a symlinked directory resolves.

M5_readdir_guard_dropped._note: The directory-level guard predates #4464. ⛔ Its first mutant run reddened NOTHING, and the honest reading was not 'defensive, drop it' but 'the axis set had no observer for it': the loop case (G10) never reaches readdirSync on a bad path, because the per-entry statSync raises ELOOP one step earlier and M4 already covers that. G11 was added for the guard's OTHER stated case — a root that is not a directory, where readdirSync raises ENOTDIR — and it is the one this mutant reddens. Written down rather than quietly deleted because the sequence (guard -> no red -> new axis -> red) is the evidence that the guard is live, and a reader who only sees the final green matrix cannot reconstruct it.
